questions.questionText: Which statement identifies why depreciation is provided on non-current assets?

options.A: so that the cost is allocated to periods that benefit from them
options.B: so that the realisation concept is applied
options.C: so that there is enough cash in the business to replace them
options.D: so that they are shown at market value

questions.questionText: New equipment costing $40000, with an estimated residual value of $6000, was acquired at the beginning of the year on 1 January. On the same date the business made the following payments in respect of the equipment. $ delivery 5000 installation 7000 8-year maintenance contract 8000 The equipment has an estimated life of 8 years. The business uses the straight-line method of depreciation. What would be the carrying amount for this item at the end of the year on 31 December?
Which error would not be identified by preparing a trial balance?

options.A: A contra entry of $650 had been entered twice in the sales ledger control account.
options.B: A purchase invoice of $495 had been recorded as $459 in the purchases journal.
options.C: Carriage inwards of $57 in the cash book had been recorded as $75 in the carriage inwards account.
options.D: Discount allowed of $35 had been credited to the discount received account.

questions.questionText: During the year a sole trader withdrew $3000 cash from the business bank account. Accounting entries made were a debit of $300 to the drawings account and a credit of $3000 to the bank account. In addition, $500 had been omitted from the discount received account in the trial balance. What was the balance on the suspense account before these errors were corrected?
A company’s bank statement showed a credit balance of $2000. The following issues were found.
Why might a business maintain a sales ledger control account as part of the double entry accounting system?
The purchases ledger control account showed a balance of $79500 before the following errors were taken into account.

A business has trade receivables of $52000 at the year-end. The allowance for irrecoverable debts in the draft statement of financial position is $3000. The allowance for irrecoverable debts is to be changed to 5% of trade receivables. What is the effect of changing the allowance? on profit on current assets

A trader prepared her financial statements but made no adjustments for accrued rent receivable at the end of the year. What is the effect of this omission? current assets current liabilities profit for the year
A sole trader calculated her draft profit for the year as $50000. She asked her accountant for advice regarding four issues which she thought might affect the draft profit.
Which items in the books of a partnership would increase the profit available for distribution to the partners?

The following information is available. $ capital: L 68000 M 102000 profit for the year before appropriation 28900 drawings: L 8000 M 12000 No interest is charged on drawings up to $10000 for each partner. Interest at a rate of 5% is charged on any drawings in excess of $10000. What was L’s share of residual profit?
Which statements describe the advantages of a rights issue of shares?

Why would employees be interested in their employer’s financial statements?

options.A: to assess whether the business can continue to trade in the foreseeable future
options.B: to compare their salaries with the employees of competitors
options.C: to put a value on the reputation of the business
options.D: to understand the impact of the business on the economy

questions.questionText: A business received a five-year loan of $40000. The loan was paid into the bank current account. What was the effect of the loan? return on current ratio capital employed

The draft financial statements of a business for the year ended 30 June included the following: $ revenue 280000 gross profit 60000 It was subsequently discovered that the closing inventory was understated by $10000. What was the gross profit margin after correcting this error?

The following information is available for a company. sales revenue for the year $1600000 debenture interest paid $60000 gross profit margin 20% operating expenses to revenue ratio 12% return on capital employed 16% What is the company’s capital employed?
What are the benefits of operating a just in time (JIT) system of inventory management?

Eight employees work in a team. Each employee is paid $16 an hour and the team share a group bonus between them, which is based on their output of product. For any production in excess of 500 units the team, as a group, is paid a bonus of $8 per unit. The bonus is shared equally and paid on a weekly basis. Last week, each member of the team worked 40 hours, and the team as a whole produced 560 units. What is the pay of each member of the team?
Which type of business is most likely to use a batch costing system?

A company is asked to make a new machine for a customer. It provides the following estimates. Materials will cost $1100. Labour will be 30 hours at a cost of $14 per hour. The company charges overheads at $10 per labour hour and has a mark-up of 30% on total cost. What is the price on the job cost sheet?

Which formula would be used to calculate an overhead absorption rate for a capital-intensive production process? labour hours A overhead costs machine hours B overhead costs overhead costs C labour hours overhead costs D machine hours
